name: Shopproof Restock: Back in Stock Alerts and Preorders for WooCommerce
author: shopproofapp

sections.description:
Shopproof Restock lets shoppers ask for one email when an out-of-stock product, or one option of it, is back. It also lets you sell a product as a preorder while it is on backorder, with the date it is delivered by shown before the purchase.

It is built for shops in the EU, where an email address needs a clear purpose and a record of consent. Technical help, not legal advice.

Back-in-stock alerts

  • A “notify me” form on out-of-stock products, placed by itself under the add-to-cart area (classic and block themes), or where you want it with the “Back-in-stock form” block or the [shopproof_restock_form] shortcode.
  • Works for single products and for each option (size, colour) of a product with options.
  • Double opt-in: on by default for shops in Germany and Austria, and a setting for everyone else. The alert only goes out after the shopper confirms.
  • A consent record for every signup: when they signed up, the exact text they saw, the language, and when they confirmed. Download it as a CSV file.
  • One alert per signup, sent in the background in batches when stock comes back. Each signup is claimed before its email goes out, so nobody gets the same alert twice.
  • Emails use your shop’s own email design and mailer, and their subject, heading and extra text can be changed under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails. Every email has a link to remove the address, and mail apps get a one-click unsubscribe.
  • A send log for the last 30 days that shows what was handed to your mailer and what it refused.
  • Shopper texts in English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Dutch, Polish and Hungarian. The form and emails follow the language the shopper sees the shop in.
  • No limits on signups or alerts for your shop. To stop misuse of the form, one visitor can sign up 10 times an hour, and an address gets one confirmation email at a time.
  • If your mailer refuses alerts (for example during a mail outage), sending stops after three refusals in a row and the rest keep waiting. You can try the refused ones again from the Restock screen.

Preorders

  • Turn on “Preorder” in a simple product’s Inventory tab and give the date (or month) by which you deliver.
  • While the product is on backorder, its button says “Preorder” and “Delivery by …” shows on the product page, in the cart and checkout (classic and block), and on the order and its emails.
  • Without a delivery date, or once that date has passed, no preorder is shown, so shoppers always know by when it comes. EU rules for online sales ask the shop to name the date by which it delivers; the wording says just that.

Set up with your AI assistant

  • Connect Claude Desktop, Cursor or another assistant that supports MCP. It sets up the form, double opt-in and preorders after you say yes, and tells you who is waiting for which product.
  • Email addresses stay hidden unless you allow them. It never sends emails, never deletes signups and cannot turn double opt-in off for shops in Germany or Austria.

What it does not do

  • It does not add anything to your newsletter. A back-in-stock alert is the one email the shopper asked for.
  • It does not tell you whether an email reached the inbox. Only your mail service knows that. If emails do not arrive, an SMTP plugin with a mail service usually fixes it.

Privacy

The plugin stores, in your own WordPress database: the shopper’s email address, the product, the language, the version of the form text they saw, and when they signed up, confirmed and got their alert. Nothing is sent to us or to any other service. Unconfirmed signups are deleted after 7 days, finished ones after a year, signups still waiting for stock after two years (or when the product is deleted), and send log lines after 30 days. To limit signups per visitor, a keyed hash of the visitor’s IP address is kept for an hour. The plugin adds itself to WordPress’s personal data export and erase tools and suggests a text for your privacy policy.

Part of Shopproof

Shopproof makes free tools for EU online shops. See also Shopproof (EU compliance hub) and Shopproof Accessibility.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin. WooCommerce must be active.
  2. Open WooCommerce > Restock and check the double opt-in setting.
  3. The form shows by itself on out-of-stock product pages. To place it yourself, turn off automatic placement and use the block or the shortcode.
  4. For a preorder, edit a simple product, open Inventory, tick “Preorder” and give a delivery date or window.
sections.faq:
Does it send emails through your servers?

No. Emails go through your shop’s own mailer (WordPress and WooCommerce), like your order emails. Nothing leaves your site except those emails.

Is double opt-in required?

That depends on your country and your lawyer. Courts in Germany treat an email to an address nobody confirmed as a risk for the shop, and Austria has a similar consent rule for advertising emails, so it is on by default in both countries. You can turn it on or off for any shop under WooCommerce > Restock > Settings. Technical help, not legal advice.

What happens when the product is back?

When its stock status changes to “In stock”, the alerts go out in the background, 25 at a time. A shopper who confirms later, while the product is in stock, gets their alert straight away. Confirming takes one press of a button on your site, so a mail scanner that opens links cannot confirm an address by itself.

Can I change the email texts?

Yes, the subject and heading under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails, and the whole email by copying the template to your theme (woocommerce/emails/shopproof-restock.php).

Does it work with page caching?

Yes. The form does not depend on a fresh page: it has no time-limited security code that a cached page would break. The page a shopper sees after confirming or removing their address is kept out of the cache, so their message is never shown to anyone else. Tested with Cache Enabler.

Can my AI assistant set this up for me?

Yes, if it is a desktop app that supports MCP (for example Claude Desktop or Cursor). Turn it on under WooCommerce > Restock > AI assistant and create a connection key. The site needs HTTPS. The key works only for the assistant connection, not for the rest of your site, and it is deleted after 90 days, when you turn the connection off or when you deactivate the plugin. On a multisite network, keys can be made only when the plugin is network active. The assistant shows you each change first, and you can undo it. Shoppers’ email addresses stay hidden from it unless you turn that on. It cannot send emails, delete signups or turn off double opt-in for a shop in Germany or Austria.
sections.changelog:
0.2.0

  • Better: the Back-in-stock form block is easier to find in the block inserter, also when you search in German, French, Italian or Dutch (“notify me”, “wieder verfügbar”, “de nouveau en stock”).
  • New: AI assistant connection (MCP), off until you turn it on under WooCommerce > Restock > AI assistant. Your own AI assistant can set up Restock and preorders and tell you who is waiting for what, always after showing you the change. Every change is listed and can be undone. Email addresses only with a separate switch. It never sends emails or deletes signups. The plugin sends nothing anywhere; the assistant connects to your shop.

0.1.0

  • First release: back-in-stock form for products and their options, double opt-in with a consent record, background alerts through your own mailer, send log, CSV export, basic preorders with the delivery date in the cart and on the order. Shopper texts in 8 languages.
